solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Put foot down after Charlie humiliated (9)

indicatorNotes.after: HASTENED comes after C, so C is written first

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
to put your foot down is to speed up

annotation.surface: Someone humiliated who takes it out on the accelerator, or finally puts their foot down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put foot down' reads as being firm; here it is pressing the accelerator. The definition sits at the end, after the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: To be chastened is to be humbled or subdued after a rebuke.

entries.clue: Sinister fellow turning up in empty city (6)

indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down clue, turning a word up writes it from bottom to top
indicatorNotes.in: the turned word goes inside the emptied city
indicatorNotes.empty: an empty word keeps only its outer letters

blocks.note: CITY with its inside removed leaves C…Y
a peer is an equal, a fellow

annotation.surface: A shady character reappearing in a deserted city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sinister fellow' looks like one phrase naming a villain; the definition is only 'Sinister', and the fellow is a peer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe what makes your skin crawl.

indicatorNotes.remarkably: done remarkably, the letters end up in an unexpected order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: Someone who fools around yet is surprisingly teetotal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mess about' looks like the anagram signal, but those words are the letters; the signal is 'remarkably'.
annotation.definitionFit: Abstemious means sparing with food and especially drink, so sober.

indicatorNotes.almost: almost the whole word: drop its last letter

blocks.note: TREAT (to nurse a patient) without its last letter
guaranteed = sure

annotation.surface: A nurse all but certain of winning an award.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prize' reads as a noun, an award; it is the verb, to value highly, matching the verb treasure.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to hold something dear and value it highly.

indicatorNotes.hiding: the answer is concealed inside the words

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of 'Hitman' through 'in' into the start of 'Japan'

annotation.surface: A question about where a Japanese assassin might be lurking.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a ninja was a covert Japanese assassin, and one is literally hiding in these words.
annotation.definitionFit: Ninjas were feudal Japanese agents hired for espionage and assassination.

entries.clue: Pleased something done about one of The Sun’s offerings (9)

indicatorNotes.about: DEED goes round, or about, the other piece

blocks.note: a deed is something done
the sun gives light

annotation.surface: Someone happy with something written about in the tabloid newspaper The Sun.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitalised 'The Sun' suggests the British tabloid; it is just the star in the sky, which offers light and heat.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with delighted the stronger of the two.

entries.clue: Nothing must be removed from ornate old boat (6)

indicatorNotes.must be removed from: take the first thing out of the second

blocks.note: baroque = highly ornate
nothing = O, the zero; taken out of BAROQUE

annotation.surface: A restorer insisting that nothing be stripped from a finely decorated old vessel.
annotation.walkthrough: O as nothing, the zero, is a standard crossword convention.
annotation.definitionFit: A barque is a sailing ship, a word now mostly found in history and poetry.

blocks.note: an action brought before a court
a protective container, as for a pillow or spectacles
what a detective works on

annotation.surface: Legal action that extends to an inquiry.
annotation.walkthrough: This is really a triple definition: 'covering' looks like a joining word but is a third meaning of case.
annotation.definitionFit: Case means a lawsuit, a detective's investigation, and a protective cover.

indicatorNotes.Disorganised: the letters are put out of order
indicatorNotes.overlooking: to overlook something is to leave it out

blocks.note: the fodder before one A is left out
one A dropped from PARALEGAL, leaving 8 letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A muddled legal assistant who fails to notice a grievance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance at a law office; it is an illness. Pellagra is a disease caused by lack of niacin.
annotation.definitionFit: A complaint can mean an ailment, and pellagra is a vitamin-deficiency disease.

indicatorNotes.returning: going back, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: a Name is an underwriter at Lloyd's of London, written backwards
had dinner = ate dinner

annotation.surface: An insurer's policy coming back after they took it on.
annotation.walkthrough: At Lloyd's of London, the insurance market, the private backers who underwrite risk are called Names.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to come out from a source, as rumours or smells do.

blocks.note: a compass-point abbreviation, as on a map
Indonesia is one example of a country in Asia, the East

annotation.surface: A single letter said to come from Indonesia.
annotation.walkthrough: Usually a lone letter is a piece of wordplay; here E is a whole definition, since E stands for eastern. 'Perhaps' flags Indonesia as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: E abbreviates eastern, and Indonesia lies in the East.

entries.clue: Silence writer making one envious at first (5)

indicatorNotes.making: the one letter is made into another

blocks.note: a quill pen writes
one = I, the Roman numeral, which is swapped out
first letter of envious, swapped in for the I

annotation.surface: An author who silences rivals by making them jealous.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is a pen, not an author: the quill. Change its I to E and QUILL becomes QUELL.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to put a stop to noise or protest.

blocks.note: journalists are the press
a gang is a gathering of people

annotation.surface: Foreign reporters meeting up in the Chinese city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shanghai' is at the end and looks like a place; it is the verb, to force someone into service, originally onto a ship.
annotation.definitionFit: To shanghai someone is to press-gang them: force them into work or service.

entries.clue: Listing showing signs of recovery, they say (7)

indicatorNotes.they say: what people say, so go by the sound

blocks.note: healing = getting better

annotation.surface: A patient on a list of those getting better.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Listing' reads as putting on a list; it is a ship leaning over to one side, which is heeling.
annotation.definitionFit: A ship that heels leans to one side, which sailors also call listing.

indicatorNotes.unusually: the letters come in an unusual order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 2 letters
anagram fodder, 8 letters, joined to MP by 'in'

annotation.surface: A Member of Parliament whose election campaign was unusually brief.
annotation.walkthrough: MP looks like an abbreviation to expand; here its two letters go straight into the anagram with ELECTION.
annotation.definitionFit: Something short of what is needed is incomplete.

entries.clue: Note Jean-Paul Sartre’s bed set on fire again (5)

blocks.note: re is a note of the scale: do, re, mi
lit is French for bed, and Sartre was French

annotation.surface: A remark that the philosopher Sartre's bed has been torched once more.
annotation.walkthrough: Sartre is only there to signal French: his bed is a lit.
annotation.definitionFit: Relit is the past tense of relight, to set burning again.

blocks.note: left the field: pulled out of the contest
odd or unconventional, a baseball term

annotation.surface: Someone finding it odd that a rival pulled out.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: to withdraw from a race is to leave the field.
annotation.definitionFit: Left-field means unconventional or odd, from the far side of a baseball field.

indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short: drop the last letter

blocks.note: PHONEY, a fake person, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A fraudster making a quick phone call.
annotation.walkthrough: A phoney is a fraud or impostor; clip it and it becomes the verb to phone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to ring someone up.

entries.clue: Woman waiting ages to run off after author (8)

blocks.note: to pen is to write, and a writer is a pen
eloping lovers run off together

annotation.surface: A woman who has waited years before running off with a writer.
annotation.walkthrough: In Homer's Odyssey, Penelope waits twenty years for Odysseus to come home, fending off suitors; the surface has her running off, which she never did.
annotation.definitionFit: Penelope is the faithful wife in the Odyssey who waits ages for her husband.

indicatorNotes.from: the answer is taken out of the next word
indicatorNotes.lying around: turned around, so read the letters backwards

blocks.note: c(ARCAS)s read backwards

annotation.surface: Bones pulled from a carcass left lying about.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a literal scene, bones from a carcass. Read CARCASS backwards (SSACRAC) and SACRA is inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Sacra is the plural of sacrum, the triangular bone at the base of the spine.

entries.clue: Misguided Republican steps in, one not in union (8)

indicatorNotes.Misguided: guided wrongly, so the letters go astray

blocks.note: R = Republican
anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A wrong-headed Republican politician intervening, perhaps in a union dispute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union; it means marriage, and a spinster is an unmarried woman.
annotation.definitionFit: A spinster is a woman who has not married, so is in no marital union.

blocks.note: a Fed is an FBI agent
to be up before a judge is to be in court

annotation.surface: A spy who is annoyed at being taken to court.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brassed off' is British slang for annoyed or fed up.
annotation.definitionFit: Brassed off and fed up both mean thoroughly annoyed.

entries.clue: New way to the top beginning to emerge (7)

blocks.note: N = new
an ascent is a climb, a route up

annotation.surface: A fresh route up a mountain starting to appear.
annotation.walkthrough: N for new is a standard abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into being.

blocks.note: the surface wants a window shutter; the setter means a flap of skin over the eye
true of window shutters at night, and of this body part every night

annotation.surface: A window shutter pulled to at bedtime.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a window shutter closed at night; the shutter is part of your face.
annotation.definitionFit: Eyelids close over the eyes like shutters when you sleep.

entries.clue: Where you might find mule travelling thus? (2,4)

blocks.note: a mule is a backless slipper, worn on the foot
walking

annotation.surface: A question about where to look for a pack animal on the move.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mule' calls up the pack animal; it is also a backless slipper or shoe, which you find on a foot.
annotation.definitionFit: Travelling thus means walking, and a mule, the slipper, is worn at the end of a leg.

entries.clue: Spooner’s nosy follower, one employed in the kitchen (6,3)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: the Reverend Spooner swapped the first sounds of words

blocks.note: prying = nosy; it takes the F from the second word
a fan is a follower; it takes the P from the first word

annotation.surface: A snooping admirer who has got a job in a restaurant kitchen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One employed' sounds like a worker; it is a utensil being used.
annotation.definitionFit: A frying pan is a piece of kitchen equipment put to use in cooking.

entries.clue: Poet turning tail, cause of ferment? (5)

indicatorNotes.turning tail: the tail, the last letters, turned round

blocks.note: W. B. Yeats, the Irish poet

annotation.surface: A poet who ran away and stirred up unrest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turning tail' means fleeing, but here the tail of YEATS, its last two letters, is turned round. 'Ferment' also means unrest, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: the fungus used in brewing and baking is what makes sugars ferment.

indicatorNotes.called out: spoken, so go by the sound

blocks.note: to bar a door is to lock it

annotation.surface: A philosopher in a pub shouting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub; it is the verb to fasten. John Locke was the English philosopher.
annotation.definitionFit: John Locke was a 17th-century English philosopher.

blocks.note: the capital of Egypt; its middle letter I goes

annotation.surface: An artist feeling discouraged in the big city.
annotation.walkthrough: Sir Anthony Caro was a British abstract sculptor.
annotation.definitionFit: Anthony Caro was a leading British sculptor.

entries.clue: Trend in Great Depression ruined Democrat: millions lost (3,4)

indicatorNotes.ruined: wrecked, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.lost: what is lost is no longer there, so the M goes missing from the word

blocks.note: the fodder before the M goes
m = millions, removed

annotation.surface: A Democratic politician financially ruined during the 1930s slump.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all economics; the definition is a design style that was in fashion during the Depression era.
annotation.definitionFit: Art Deco was the dominant decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s.

indicatorNotes.nearly: not quite all: drop the last letter

blocks.note: a part is a section
I = one, the Roman numeral, as in Part I
ALL without its last letter

annotation.surface: Nearly all of the opening section is biased.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First section' reads as Part I; the numeral follows PART in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Partial means biased, favouring one side.

entries.clue: Cleaner put off man of good birth (9)

blocks.note: to deter is to put off
gent, short for gentleman

annotation.surface: A domestic cleaner who discouraged a well-born suitor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' at the front reads as a person who cleans; it is the substance, a cleaning agent.
annotation.definitionFit: A cleaner can be a product rather than a person, and detergent is one such product.
